app_commands.note: repeat_interval 1, the same as APP-TELEGRAM: this interval is checked once per run of the app, so it is a floor under every task inside it - at 60 a task whose own time_window asked for 60 s ran every 60-120 s depending on phase, and nothing in that task's config said why. The app exits immediately when nothing is due.

timeout 2400s, not 600: this is the budget for the whole collection pass, so it has to stay above the slowest metric in it plus the rest of the pass (MAINTENANCE_INDEX_FRAGMENTATION alone is allowed 1800s). Keep this number ABOVE the largest metric timeout. Since 0.30.0 a pass runs each category of each server as a batch of its own, and a batch is claimed by one pass at a time, so the command is async - a pass that holds one slow batch (the nightly index-fragmentation scan took 1009 s on the largest instance and held INSTANCE_STATUS of every server for ~18 minutes, because a sync command starts no new pass) no longer stops the next pass; repeat_interval 1 as APP-SQL_TASKS and APP-BACKUP-RESTORE; max_parallel 4 is the brake on how many passes are alive; a pass that finds nothing due exits without writing a run row.
Generates scheduled report summaries every 30 seconds. Runs synchronously so one report generation pass completes before the next begins.
Evaluates SLA and SLO compliance every 5 minutes across the estate. A 5-minute burn window requires runs at least that often, and a full evaluation takes ~25s.
repeat_interval 1: polls and processes queued Telegram messages every second. Runs synchronously with rapid exits when no messages are queued.

app_commands.display_name: Serve inventory report over HTTP (web host)
app_commands.command_text: python -m dbabrain.webhost.cli --config config.json serve --root runtime/reports --mount report_dba --port 8080
app_commands.note: On by default: the reports and the console on port 8080. A service, not a job - repeat 0, retry 0 and timeout 0 mean start once, never kill, restart at once if it stops. It shipped off until 2026-09-11 because `daemon --once` waited on it for ever; --once now skips a timeout-0 service and says so, so switching it on no longer costs the single pass.

On by default, and idle until data/restore_config.json declares a backup or a restore: init writes that file with both lists empty, and an empty list is 'nothing configured' - status done, no work, no alert. Nothing is backed up or restored until an entry is added. repeat_interval 1 since 0.24.0, as APP-SQL_TASKS - down from 30 (2026-09-21) and 300 before it. This app's interval is a FLOOR under every job inside it, because one run works through its own due list one job at a time: at 300 a log backup declared at 900 s ran every ~1200 s. And it is what decides how many jobs due at the same moment run at once: each async run takes the due jobs no other run has started, so at 30 s the second started 30 s after the first and three due restores reached two at once (measured on the 0.23.0 soak). At 1 s the next run starts a second later and takes the next job, up to max_parallel. 1 costs one short process a second that exits at once when nothing is due, and it is safe only because run_mode async is paired with the claim: ux_job_runs_claim accepts one running row per backup job, so a second process is told the work is taken.

app_commands.display_name: Watch dbabrain itself: alert on an app that starts failing, summarise every app hourly
app_commands.note: The one app that watches the others, and the one that must not depend on them. It reads job_runs directly and resolves its own chat from telegram_groups.json, so an estate where every other app is failing is exactly the estate it still reports from. Runs around the clock every 60s: the failure alert fires the moment an app command goes from working to failing, at any hour, while the app-by-app summary is confined to 08:00-20:00 local and one per hour (both decided inside ops-status, not by this schedule). Added 2026-08-13 after a NameError stopped every scheduled SQL task for a day with nothing to notice it - see dbabrain/db/ops_status.py.

notes: node_role is 'all' here so a single-machine install works as copied: 'all' runs on any node. A two-node estate sets 'master' or 'worker' per command and declares each node's role with the DBABRAIN_NODE_ROLE environment variable - it is deliberately not in config.json, so a config copied between nodes cannot mislabel one.

Every command is active out of the box, and every one of them must finish status=done on an install where init has run and nothing else has - no inventory, no token, no restore entry, no SQL task. Missing configuration is a state the app reports and skips, never a failure: a default schedule that errors every cycle on a correct install teaches its reader to ignore the log. tests/test_every_app_command_runs_on_an_unconfigured_install.py holds every entry here to that. Set active: false to switch one off.
